expectations.text: Asks targeted clarifying questions in Portuguese covering at least: the current pain and why migrate now, measurable goals, alternatives, trade-offs, and impacted teams
expectations.evidence: DESIGN-DOC Section 0 ('Perguntas em aberto') lists 16 questions in Portuguese grouped by theme. Current pain / why migrate now: Q1 'Por que migrar agora? Qual e a dor concreta? (ex.: deploys lentos, time travado por acoplamento, escala...)' and Q3 (restricao de prazo). Measurable goals: Q2 'Quais metricas de sucesso definem que a migracao valeu a pena? (frequencia de deploy, lead time, MTTR, custo, onboarding)'. Alternatives + trade-offs: Section 2.3 alternatives table + Section 2.2 'Reflexao honesta antes de seguir: microsservicos nao sao automaticamente melhores... trocam complexidade interna por complexidade operacional distribuida'. Impacted teams: Q11 'Quantas pessoas no time... Como estao organizados os times?', Q12 (experiencia com distribuidos), Q13 (plataforma/infra). response.md also restates 5 key questions including 'Por que migrar agora?' and team size/experience. All content is in Portuguese.

(ex.: Rails, Django, Spring, .NET, Node, Laravel)'. Section 4.2 explicitly refuses to name services: 'As fronteiras concretas dependem das respostas as perguntas 9 e 10... Sem essa informacao, listar servicos especificos aqui seria invencao.' Section 8.3 'Nao estimei datas porque seriam numeros inventados.' No metrics, team names, or domain boundaries are asserted as facts. The DRAFT header warning states 'Nao inventei numeros, nomes de servicos, tecnologias ou prazos.' Reference books (Fowler, Newman, Evans) are real external sources, not fabricated project facts.

expectations.text: Does not deliver a finished design doc: if any file is created it contains only structure with explicit pending markers and zero invented content
expectations.evidence: A file WAS created (DESIGN-DOC-migracao-microservicos.md, 12k). The 'zero invented content' conjunct is satisfied (no fabricated project facts; project-specific fields use _(preencher)_). However the 'contains only structure with explicit pending markers' conjunct is NOT satisfied: several sections deliver fully-written, committed methodological content rather than skeleton-with-markers. Section 4.1 fully specifies the Strangler Fig procedure (5 steps + mermaid diagram), Section 4.2 gives concrete boundary-prioritization criteria, Section 5.2 commits to saga/outbox/CDC patterns, Section 7 lists non-negotiable observability requirements, and Section 9 'Riscos e mitigacoes' is a fully-populated table with concrete risks AND mitigations (no _(preencher)_ markers). This is substantially more than a structural template with pending markers - it reads as a near-complete generic design doc. While not project-specific invention, it goes beyond 'only structure', failing the stated bar.

suggestions.assertion: Does not deliver a finished design doc: if any file is created it contains only structure with explicit pending markers and zero invented content
suggestions.reason: This assertion bundles two distinct properties: (a) 'only structure with pending markers' and (b) 'zero invented content'. A reasonable executor can satisfy (b) perfectly while pre-filling generic, non-project-specific methodology (Strangler Fig steps, a populated risk/mitigation table, observability requirements) - which is arguably good behavior, not a failure. The conjunction makes the verdict ambiguous and penalizes useful generic guidance. Consider splitting into two assertions: one checking 'no project-specific facts are fabricated (stack, metrics, domain boundaries, team names, dates)' and a separate, clearer one such as 'project-specific sections are left as explicit pending markers rather than filled with assumptions'. That isolates the behavior you actually care about and removes the gray zone around generic best-practice content.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-3 are well-targeted and discriminating. Assertion 4 is the weak one - its two-part wording creates a genuine gray area (generic methodology vs. invented project facts) that makes pass/fail subjective; splitting it would make grading deterministic.
